title: Moments of inertia of trunk segments of living males by MRI

quantity.name: segment moment of inertia about CM
quantity.definition: principal-axis moments of inertia about segment CM; x = transverse (medio-lateral), y = antero-posterior, z = longitudinal

source.authors: Pearsall DJ, Reid JG, Ross R
source.sample: 26 males; 26 living adult males, MRI (Philips 1.5 T), prone, arms above head; 10-mm slices every 50 mm
source.notes: height SD 5.7 cm; body mass SD 16.8 kg (range 56.4-129 kg); BMI 28.6 ± 4.8 (range 19.7-39.3). DOI not printed in PDF (likely 10.1007/BF02368294 – verify).

protocol.summary: Moments of inertia of thorax, abdomen, pelvis and whole trunk about their CM.
how_to_use: Use Ix (about the medio-lateral axis, i.e. the flexion axis) for sagittal dynamics: whole trunk 2.1 kg·m² mean (males, mean 87 kg).
Scale with body mass for other subjects (all I values correlated with body mass, r2 >= 0.74, Table 2).
Values converted from printed g·cm²×10^k to kg·m² (1 g·cm² = 1e-7 kg·m²); 'printed' keeps the original.

measurement.device: Philips Gyroscan 1.5 T; tissue densities assigned per pixel (cortical bone 1.8, cancellous 1.1, viscera/muscle/blood 1.06, adipose 0.96, lung 0.25 g/cc)

protocol.notes: Thorax = suprasternal notch (~T4/5) to xiphoid (~T9); abdomen = xiphoid to umbilicus (~L3/4); pelvis = umbilicus to pubic symphysis/greater trochanter (incl. perineum, excl. thighs); trunk = sum. Boundaries follow Zatsiorsky & Seluyanov gamma-scan definitions (thus close to de Leva UPT/MPT/LPT).

extraction.check_notes: Checked against rendered Table 1. Printed thorax Iy max 26.0 and Iz max 31.0 (×10^6 g·cm²) are inconsistent with mean/SD (probably 2.6 and 3.1) – kept as printed (converted).

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
